name: Acoustic Materials
tagline: Absorption and insulation — two different problems, two different products
description: Absorption stops a room echoing; insulation stops sound getting between rooms. Confusing the two is the most common mistake in interior acoustics — foam on a wall will never stop your neighbour's television. Every product here states which job it does and its NRC or STC rating.

materials.name: Acoustic wall panel
materials.blurb: Fabric or felt panels that soak up reverberation (NRC 0.6–0.95)
materials.description: Absorptive panels placed at first reflection points calm a room's echo and make speech intelligible. Coverage of 20–30% of wall area is usually enough — full coverage is wasted money.

materials.name: PET acoustic panel
materials.blurb: Recycled polyester felt — cuttable, colourful, no fibres
materials.description: Made from recycled bottles, PET felt cuts with a knife, sheds no fibres and comes in strong colours. It has become the default for offices, ceilings baffles and desk screens.

materials.name: Fabric acoustic panel
materials.blurb: Upholstered absorber that reads as a design element
materials.description: An absorptive core wrapped in fabric, so acoustics arrive looking like panelling rather than equipment. Choose an acoustically transparent fabric or the panel stops working.

materials.name: Wooden acoustic panel
materials.blurb: Slatted or perforated timber over an absorptive backing
materials.description: The finish that lets a room look like a library and perform like a studio. Absorption depends on the open area between slats and the felt behind — the timber itself does little.

materials.name: Acoustic ceiling tile
materials.blurb: Mineral or metal tiles that treat the largest surface in the room
materials.description: The ceiling is usually the biggest uninterrupted surface available, which makes it the most efficient place to add absorption. Combine a high-NRC tile with carpet and the room settles immediately.

materials.name: Acoustic baffle
materials.blurb: Vertical fins hung from the slab — absorption on two faces
materials.description: Suspended baffles absorb from both sides and leave services exposed, which suits industrial-style offices and restaurants. Spacing controls both the acoustic effect and the visual rhythm.

materials.name: Acoustic cloud
materials.blurb: Horizontal absorptive raft floating below the slab
materials.description: A suspended panel placed directly above the noise source — a meeting table, a dining area — giving local absorption without a full ceiling. Efficient because both faces work.

materials.name: Soundproof door
materials.blurb: Sealed heavy leaf rated by STC — stops sound, not echo
materials.description: Mass plus perimeter seals plus a drop seal at the threshold. A studio door is only as good as its weakest gap, so the frame and seals matter as much as the leaf.

materials.name: Rockwool insulation
materials.blurb: Mineral wool slab that fills partitions and blocks transmission
materials.description: Dense stone wool packed into a stud partition or ceiling void raises the STC substantially and is non-combustible. The workhorse of interior sound insulation.

materials.name: Glass wool insulation
materials.blurb: Lighter mineral wool for ducts, ceilings and general infill
materials.description: Cheaper and lighter than rockwool with slightly lower density, so it is used for ducting, ceiling voids and general thermal-plus-acoustic work. Always install behind a proper facing.
